statement.p: Evaluate the line integral \int_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{F} \cdot \,d\ \mathbf{r} where \mathbf{F}=\left\lt 4 \sin x, -4 \cos y, xz \right> and \mathcal{C} is the path given by \mathbf{r}(t) = ( t^3, t^2, -3 t) for 0 \le t \le 1

static.solution:
\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) = \left\lt 4 \sin ( t^3), -4 \cos ( t^2), -3 t^4 \right> \mathbf{r} '(t) = \left\lt 3 t^2, 2 t, -3 \right > \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r} '(t) = \left\lt 4 \sin ( t^3), -4 \cos ( t^2), -3 t^4 \right> \cdot \left\lt 3 t^2, 2 t, -3 \right > =12 t^2 \sin ( t^3) - 8 t \cos ( t^2) + 9 t^4
The line integral is then: \int_{\mathcal{C}} \mathbf{F} \cdot \,d\ \mathbf{r} = \int^1_0 \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r} '(t) \ dt = \int^1_0 12 t^2 \sin ( t^3) - 8 t \cos ( t^2) + 9 t^4\ dt = \left [ -4 \cos ( t^3) - 4 \sin ( t^2) + \frac{9}{5} t^5 \right ]^1_0 = -4 \cos (1) - 4 \sin (1) + \frac{29}{5}
